  PRACTICE MATERIAL



Diagnostics Pop Quizzes
21 quizzes - one per course - 10 multiple-choice questions each. 210 questions total.

Quizzes follow the course and module order on the diagnostics completion sheet (21 courses, 89 modules).
Each question is tagged with the module it tests. All answer keys are separate - they are grouped at the
back of this pack, after all 21 quizzes, so the quizzes can be printed without the answers.

How to use: Take one quiz after finishing a course. Score it using the separate Answer Key section at the
back, review every miss, then retake it on a later date. Target: 9 / 10 before moving on.

Quiz 2. Engine Misfire Diagnostics - 4 modules           modules

Diagnostics Pop Quizzes - Practice Material                                                                    Cover
QUIZ 1 OF 21

Course 1: Mastering Onboard Diagnostics

Name:                      Date:                  Score: ___ / 10

  Modules covered (8):
     Strategy Based Diagnostics
     Onboard Diagnostics Generation One
     Onboard Diagnostics Key Elements
     Onboard Diagnostics Key Elements Two
     Understanding Diagnostic Trouble Codes
     Understanding Drive Cycles
     Drive Cycles Diagnostics
     Control Module Power and Ground Circuit Checks

1. In Strategy Based Diagnostics, what does the diagnostic trouble code actually tell you?
Module: Strategy Based Diagnostics
  A. The fault area and the conditions the module detected - it is the starting point for testing, not proof that a
  named part has failed
  B. The exact part to replace without further testing
  C. That the fault is intermittent and can be ignored
  D. That the wiring has already been proven good
2. You start work on a case covered by Onboard Diagnostics Generation One. What is the correct first
step?
Module: Onboard Diagnostics Generation One
  A. Replace the most commonly failed part for that code
  B. Clear the codes and return the vehicle
  C. Disconnect the battery and wait for the relearn
  D. Verify the complaint, check for DTCs and freeze-frame data, and review service information for that system
3. When testing for Onboard Diagnostics Key Elements, which measurement approach gives a trustworthy
result?
Module: Onboard Diagnostics Key Elements
  A. Rely on the code description instead of measuring
  B. Back-probe every wire until one reads battery voltage
  C. Measure under the conditions that set the fault, compare to specification, and watch the live reading change
  as conditions change
  D. Measure once, key off, on a cold engine only
4. A confirmed fault in Onboard Diagnostics Key Elements Two most directly points to which cause?
Module: Onboard Diagnostics Key Elements Two
  A. Old engine oil changing the electrical signal
  B. A circuit, connection or component fault in that system, proven by measuring the circuit rather than guessing
  from the code alone
  C. A discharged battery on every vehicle with this code
  D. Low tire pressure changing the module calculation
5. On a scan tool, what should you check first for Understanding Diagnostic Trouble Codes?
Module: Understanding Diagnostic Trouble Codes
   A. The related live data PID against a known-good value, plus freeze frame and any related codes set at the
   same time
   B. Only the odometer reading
Diagnostics Pop Quizzes - Practice Material                                                     Quiz 1 - Questions 1-5
   C. The radio volume PID
   D. Whether the code can be cleared from the home screen
QUIZ 1 - CONTINUED

Course 1: Mastering Onboard Diagnostics

6. Before condemning a component in Understanding Drive Cycles, which wiring check is essential?
Module: Understanding Drive Cycles
  A. Wiggle the harness once and replace the part if nothing changes
  B. Check only the fuse and stop there
  C. Spray every connector with water and watch for a change
  D. Inspect the connector for spread, corroded or backed-out terminals, then load-test or voltage-drop the power,
  ground and signal circuits
7. What component-level test best supports a diagnosis in Drive Cycles Diagnostics?
Module: Drive Cycles Diagnostics
  A. Hit the component lightly and listen for a rattle only
  B. Read the part number and order a replacement on that alone
  C. Test the component against its specification - resistance, signal output or response to a commanded change -
  and compare it with the circuit tests already done
  D. Swap in a part from another vehicle and hope the code stays away
8. During a Control Module Power and Ground Circuit Checks case, which practice should be avoided?
Module: Control Module Power and Ground Circuit Checks
  A. Road testing after a repair
  B. Parts swapping without test results, because it can mask the fault, add new faults, and waste the customer's
  money
  C. Recording measurements before clearing codes
  D. Checking service information and TSBs
9. After repairing a fault found under Strategy Based Diagnostics, how do you verify the repair?
Module: Strategy Based Diagnostics
  A. Clear the codes, run the drive cycle or operating conditions that enable the monitor, and confirm the monitor
  runs and passes with no code returning
  B. Clear the codes in the bay and release the vehicle immediately
  C. Drive around the block once with the scan tool disconnected
  D. Turn the warning lamp bulb check off
10. Two tests disagree during Onboard Diagnostics Generation One - the live data looks normal but the
fault returns under load. What is the best next move?
Module: Onboard Diagnostics Generation One
  A. Replace both the sensor and the module at once
  B. Tell the customer the fault is normal
  C. Erase the code history so it cannot return
  D. Recreate the exact freeze-frame conditions and graph or record the data through the fault, checking for
  dropouts and intermittent connections

Course 2: Engine Misfire Diagnostics

Name:                       Date:                    Score: ___ / 10

  Modules covered (4):
      Engine Misfire Monitoring
      Under Minded Misfire Diagnostics

1. You start work on a case covered by Engine Misfire Monitoring. What is the correct first step?
Module: Engine Misfire Monitoring
  A. Clear the codes and return the vehicle
  B. Disconnect the battery and wait for the relearn
  C. Verify the complaint, check for DTCs and freeze-frame data, and review service information for that system
  D. Replace the most commonly failed part for that code
2. When testing for Under Minded Misfire Diagnostics, which measurement approach gives a trustworthy
result?
Module: Under Minded Misfire Diagnostics
  A. Back-probe every wire until one reads battery voltage
  B. Measure under the conditions that set the fault, compare to specification, and watch the live reading change
  as conditions change
  C. Measure once, key off, on a cold engine only
  D. Rely on the code description instead of measuring
3. A confirmed fault in Automotive Thermal Imaging and Diagnostics most directly points to which cause?
Module: Automotive Thermal Imaging and Diagnostics
  A. A circuit, connection or component fault in that system, proven by measuring the circuit rather than guessing
  from the code alone
  B. A discharged battery on every vehicle with this code
  C. Low tire pressure changing the module calculation
  D. Old engine oil changing the electrical signal
4. On a scan tool, what should you check first for Knock Sensor Voltage High?
Module: Knock Sensor Voltage High
  A. Only the odometer reading
  B. The radio volume PID
  C. Whether the code can be cleared from the home screen
  D. The related live data PID against a known-good value, plus freeze frame and any related codes set at the
  same time
5. Before condemning a component in Engine Misfire Monitoring, which wiring check is essential?
Module: Engine Misfire Monitoring
  A. Check only the fuse and stop there
  B. Spray every connector with water and watch for a change
  C. Inspect the connector for spread, corroded or backed-out terminals, then load-test or voltage-drop the power,
  ground and signal circuits
  D. Wiggle the harness once and replace the part if nothing changes

  conditions
  D. A discharged battery on every vehicle with this code

Module: Cam Position Actuator Valve Positive Control
  A. Recording measurements before clearing codes
  B. Checking service information and TSBs
  C. Road testing after a repair
  D. Parts swapping without test results, because it can mask the fault, add new faults, and waste the customer's
  money
3. After repairing a fault found under Camshaft Position Sensor Voltage Low, how do you verify the repair?
Module: Camshaft Position Sensor Voltage Low
  A. Drive around the block once with the scan tool disconnected
  B. Turn the warning lamp bulb check off
  C. Clear the codes, run the drive cycle or operating conditions that enable the monitor, and confirm the monitor
  runs and passes with no code returning
  D. Clear the codes in the bay and release the vehicle immediately
4. Two tests disagree during Camshaft Position Sensor Voltage High - the live data looks normal but the
fault returns under load. What is the best next move?
Module: Camshaft Position Sensor Voltage High
  A. Erase the code history so it cannot return
  B. Recreate the exact freeze-frame conditions and graph or record the data through the fault, checking for
  dropouts and intermittent connections
  C. Replace both the sensor and the module at once
  D. Tell the customer the fault is normal
5. In Cam Position Actuator Valve Negative Control, what does the diagnostic trouble code actually tell
you?
Module: Cam Position Actuator Valve Negative Control
  A. That the fault is intermittent and can be ignored
  B. That the wiring has already been proven good
  C. The fault area and the conditions the module detected - it is the starting point for testing, not proof that a
  named part has failed
  D. The exact part to replace without further testing

trustworthy result?
Module: Camshaft Position Sensor Voltage Low
  A. Measure under the conditions that set the fault, compare to specification, and watch the live reading change
  as conditions change
  B. Measure once, key off, on a cold engine only
  C. Rely on the code description instead of measuring
  D. Back-probe every wire until one reads battery voltage
8. A confirmed fault in Camshaft Position Sensor Voltage High most directly points to which cause?
Module: Camshaft Position Sensor Voltage High
  A. A discharged battery on every vehicle with this code
  B. Low tire pressure changing the module calculation
  C. Old engine oil changing the electrical signal
  D. An open signal ground/return, a short to voltage on the signal circuit, or a lost sensor ground holding the signal
  high
9. On a scan tool, what should you check first for Cam Position Actuator Valve Negative Control?
Module: Cam Position Actuator Valve Negative Control
  A. The radio volume PID
  B. Whether the code can be cleared from the home screen
  C. The related live data PID against a known-good value, plus freeze frame and any related codes set at the
  same time
  D. Only the odometer reading
10. Before condemning a component in Cam Position Actuator Valve Positive Control, which wiring check
is essential?
Module: Cam Position Actuator Valve Positive Control
  A. Spray every connector with water and watch for a change
  B. Inspect the connector for spread, corroded or backed-out terminals, then load-test or voltage-drop the power,
  ground and signal circuits
  C. Wiggle the harness once and replace the part if nothing changes
  D. Check only the fuse and stop there

Course 19: Accelerator Pedal Position Diagnostics

6. A confirmed fault in Accelerator Pedal Position Signal Not Plausible most directly points to which cause?
Module: Accelerator Pedal Position Signal Not Plausible
  A. A discharged battery on every vehicle with this code
  B. Low tire pressure changing the module calculation
  C. Old engine oil changing the electrical signal
  D. A biased, drifting or intermittent signal that stays in range electrically but does not match actual operating
  conditions
7. On a scan tool, what should you check first for Accelerator Pedal Position Signal Voltage Low?
Module: Accelerator Pedal Position Signal Voltage Low
  A. The radio volume PID
  B. Whether the code can be cleared from the home screen
  C. The related live data PID against a known-good value, plus freeze frame and any related codes set at the
  same time
  D. Only the odometer reading
8. Before condemning a component in Accelerator Pedal Position Signal Voltage High, which wiring check
is essential?
Module: Accelerator Pedal Position Signal Voltage High
  A. Spray every connector with water and watch for a change
  B. Inspect the connector for spread, corroded or backed-out terminals, then load-test or voltage-drop the power,
  ground and signal circuits
  C. Wiggle the harness once and replace the part if nothing changes
  D. Check only the fuse and stop there
9. What component-level test best supports a diagnosis in Accelerator Pedal Position Diagnostics?
Module: Accelerator Pedal Position Diagnostics
  A. Test the component against its specification - resistance, signal output or response to a commanded change -
  and compare it with the circuit tests already done
  B. Swap in a part from another vehicle and hope the code stays away
  C. Hit the component lightly and listen for a rattle only
  D. Read the part number and order a replacement on that alone
10. During a Accelerator Pedal Position Signal Not Plausible case, which practice should be avoided?
Module: Accelerator Pedal Position Signal Not Plausible
  A. Recording measurements before clearing codes
  B. Checking service information and TSBs
  C. Road testing after a repair
  D. Parts swapping without test results, because it can mask the fault, add new faults, and waste the customer's
  money




Diagnostics Pop Quizzes - Practice Material                                                       Quiz 19 - Questions 6-10
QUIZ 20 OF 21

Course 20: Electronic Stability Program Diagnostics

Name:                       Date:                    Score: ___ / 10

  Modules covered (3):
      Steering and Angle Sensor Voltage High Diagnostics
      YAW Sensor Communication Fault
      ESP Bus Diagnostics

1. Two tests disagree during Steering and Angle Sensor Voltage High Diagnostics - the live data looks
normal but the fault returns under load. What is the best next move?
Module: Steering and Angle Sensor Voltage High Diagnostics
  A. Recreate the exact freeze-frame conditions and graph or record the data through the fault, checking for
  dropouts and intermittent connections
  B. Replace both the sensor and the module at once
  C. Tell the customer the fault is normal
  D. Erase the code history so it cannot return
2. In YAW Sensor Communication Fault, what does the diagnostic trouble code actually tell you?
Module: YAW Sensor Communication Fault
  A. That the wiring has already been proven good
  B. The fault area and the conditions the module detected - it is the starting point for testing, not proof that a
  named part has failed
  C. The exact part to replace without further testing
  D. That the fault is intermittent and can be ignored
3. You start work on a case covered by ESP Bus Diagnostics. What is the correct first step?
Module: ESP Bus Diagnostics
  A. Verify the complaint, check for DTCs and freeze-frame data, and review service information for that system
  B. Replace the most commonly failed part for that code
  C. Clear the codes and return the vehicle
  D. Disconnect the battery and wait for the relearn
4. When testing for Steering and Angle Sensor Voltage High Diagnostics, which measurement approach
gives a trustworthy result?
Module: Steering and Angle Sensor Voltage High Diagnostics
  A. Measure once, key off, on a cold engine only
  B. Rely on the code description instead of measuring
  C. Back-probe every wire until one reads battery voltage
  D. Measure under the conditions that set the fault, compare to specification, and watch the live reading change
  as conditions change
5. A confirmed fault in YAW Sensor Communication Fault most directly points to which cause?
Module: YAW Sensor Communication Fault
  A. Low tire pressure changing the module calculation
  B. Old engine oil changing the electrical signal
  C. A wiring, terminating-resistor, power/ground or module fault on the network that stops clean data transfer
  D. A discharged battery on every vehicle with this code

  C. Only the odometer reading
  D. The radio volume PID

  B. Wiggle the harness once and replace the part if nothing changes
  C. Check only the fuse and stop there
  D. Spray every connector with water and watch for a change

Module: YAW Sensor Communication Fault
  A. Swap in a part from another vehicle and hope the code stays away
  B. Hit the component lightly and listen for a rattle only
  C. Read the part number and order a replacement on that alone
  D. Test the component against its specification - resistance, signal output or response to a commanded change -

verify the repair?
Module: Steering and Angle Sensor Voltage High Diagnostics
  A. Turn the warning lamp bulb check off
  B. Clear the codes, run the drive cycle or operating conditions that enable the monitor, and confirm the monitor
  runs and passes with no code returning
  C. Clear the codes in the bay and release the vehicle immediately
  D. Drive around the block once with the scan tool disconnected

Answer Key
All answer keys for the 21 diagnostics pop quizzes, grouped Quiz 1 through Quiz 21.

This section starts after all 21 quizzes, on its own page, so the quiz pages can be printed on their own without
the answers. Each quiz key gives the correct letter and a brief explanation for all 10 questions, plus a retake
date and second-score line for that quiz.

Target for every quiz: 9 / 10 before moving on. Review every miss against the module named in the key,
then retake the full quiz - not just the missed questions.

KEYS IN THIS SECTION
Quiz 1. Mastering Onboard Diagnostics                      Quiz 11. Fuel System Diagnostics
Quiz 2. Engine Misfire Diagnostics                         Quiz 12. FRP Sensor Diagnostics
Quiz 3. NVH Principles and Diagnostics                     Quiz 13. Diesel Pressure Regulator Diagnostics
Quiz 4. Starter Relay Diagnostics                          Quiz 14. Turbocharger Diagnostics
Quiz 5. Oil Pressure Sensor Diagnostics                    Quiz 15. Oxygen Sensor Diagnostics
Quiz 6. Crankshaft Sensor Diagnostics                      Quiz 16. EGR Diagnostics
Quiz 7. Camshaft Sensor Diagnostics                        Quiz 17. DPF Pressure Sensor Diagnostics
Quiz 8. MAF Sensor Diagnostics                             Quiz 18. Vehicle Network Diagnostics
Quiz 9. MAP and BARO Sensor Diagnostics                    Quiz 19. Accelerator Pedal Position Diagnostics
Quiz 10. IAT Sensor Diagnostics                            Quiz 20. Electronic Stability Program Diagnostics

Diagnostics Pop Quizzes - Answer Key (Separate Section)                                            Answer Key - Start
ANSWER KEY - QUIZ 1 OF 21

Course 1: Mastering Onboard Diagnostics

 Q       Answer     Why

 1       A          A code sets when a test fails under set conditions. It directs testing; it does not condemn a part by
                    itself.
                    Module: Strategy Based Diagnostics

 2       D          Strategy-based work starts with verification and data. Freeze frame shows the conditions when the
                    fault set.
                    Module: Onboard Diagnostics Generation One

 3       C          Faults are condition-dependent. Testing under the set conditions and comparing to spec separates a
                    real fault from a one-off reading.
                    Module: Onboard Diagnostics Key Elements

 4       B          The fault description narrows the cause. Confirm it with voltage, resistance and live-data checks
                    before replacing anything.
                    Module: Onboard Diagnostics Key Elements Two

 5       A          Related PIDs, freeze frame and companion codes show whether the fault is in the sensor, the circuit,
                    or a shared power/ground.
                    Module: Understanding Diagnostic Trouble Codes

 6       D          Many 'failed parts' are terminal and voltage-drop problems. A circuit that cannot carry load will make
                    a good part read faulty.
                    Module: Understanding Drive Cycles

 7       C          A component is condemned only when its own measured output is out of specification on circuits
                    already proven good.
                    Module: Drive Cycles Diagnostics

 8       B          Untested parts swapping destroys the evidence in the original fault and makes the next diagnosis
                    harder, not easier.
                    Module: Control Module Power and Ground Circuit Checks

 9       A          Verification means the enabling monitor actually ran. A cleared code that has not re-run its monitor is
                    not a proven repair.
                    Module: Strategy Based Diagnostics

 10      D          Intermittent and load-dependent faults show up only under their set conditions. Graphing through the
                    event captures the dropout.
                    Module: Onboard Diagnostics Generation One


Score: ___ / 10 Target: 9 / 10 before moving on.

Retake date: ______________________               Second score: ___ / 10

Review every miss against the module named in the key, then retake the full quiz - not just the missed questions.

                    Module: Mass Airflow Sensor Signal Voltage High

 10      D          A component is condemned only when its own measured output is out of specification on circuits
                    already proven good.
                    Module: Mass Airflow Sensor Signal Performance

Course 9: MAP and BARO Sensor Diagnostics

 Q       Answer     Why

 1       A          Verification means the enabling monitor actually ran. A cleared code that has not re-run its monitor is
                    not a proven repair.
                    Module: MAP Sensor Signal Performance

 2       D          Intermittent and load-dependent faults show up only under their set conditions. Graphing through the
                    event captures the dropout.
                    Module: MAP Sensor Pull Up Voltage Low

 3       A          A code sets when a test fails under set conditions. It directs testing; it does not condemn a part by
                    itself.
                    Module: MAP Sensor Pull Up Voltage High

 4       D          Strategy-based work starts with verification and data. Freeze frame shows the conditions when the
                    fault set.
                    Module: MAP Sensor Pull Down Type Voltage Low

 5       C          Faults are condition-dependent. Testing under the set conditions and comparing to spec separates a
                    real fault from a one-off reading.
                    Module: MAP Sensor Pull Down Type Voltage High

 6       B          The fault description narrows the cause. Confirm it with voltage, resistance and live-data checks
                    before replacing anything.
                    Module: Barometric Sensor Signal Faults

 7       A          Related PIDs, freeze frame and companion codes show whether the fault is in the sensor, the circuit,
                    or a shared power/ground.
                    Module: Barometric Sensor Shorts to Volt and Ground

 8       D          Many 'failed parts' are terminal and voltage-drop problems. A circuit that cannot carry load will make
                    a good part read faulty.
                    Module: MAP Sensor Signal Performance

 9       C          A component is condemned only when its own measured output is out of specification on circuits
                    already proven good.
                    Module: MAP Sensor Pull Up Voltage Low

 10      B          Untested parts swapping destroys the evidence in the original fault and makes the next diagnosis
                    harder, not easier.
                    Module: MAP Sensor Pull Up Voltage High
